alfriston.heading: ALFRISTON (Lord Gwydyr's Newtown Pippin; Oldaker's New; Shepherd's Pippin; Shepherd's Seedling)
alfriston.flavour: Flesh, yellowish white, crisp, juicy, sugary, and briskly flavoured.
alfriston.quality: one of the largest and best culinary apples
alfriston.storage: It comes into use in the beginning of November and continues till April.
alfriston.climate: on strong soils that are not well drained it is apt to canker.
alfriston.note: Raised by Shepherd at Uckfield, Sussex; named Alfriston after specimens sent by Mr. Brooker of Alfriston.

american-summer-pearmain.heading: AMERICAN SUMMER PEARMAIN (Early Summer Pearmain)
american-summer-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, yellow, very tender, rich, and pleasantly flavoured.
american-summer-pearmain.quality: An excellent early apple, either for dessert or kitchen use.
american-summer-pearmain.storage: It is ripe in the end of August, and will keep till the end of September.
american-summer-pearmain.climate: The tree is a healthy grower, a prolific bearer, and succeeds well on light soils.

api-etoile.heading: API ETOILE (Pomme Etoilee; Sternapfel)
api-etoile.storage: ripens about the middle or end of September.
api-etoile.note: Short entry: a much-flattened, five-angled, star-shaped variety of the Api. Hogg says the tree received under this name by the Horticultural Society was wrong (Api Petit).

baumanns-reinette.heading: BAUMANN'S REINETTE
baumanns-reinette.flavour: Flesh, white, crisp, juicy, and with a pleasant aroma.
baumanns-reinette.quality: A good but not high-class dessert apple.
baumanns-reinette.storage: It is ripe in the end of November, and keeps till March.
baumanns-reinette.note: Raised by MM. Baumann of Bolwyller, Alsace.

baxters-pearmain.heading: BAXTER'S PEARMAIN
baxters-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, yellowish, firm, brisk, and sugary, and with an abundance of pleasantly acid juice.
baxters-pearmain.quality: An excellent apple, suitable either for culinary purposes or the dessert
baxters-pearmain.storage: in use from November to March.
baxters-pearmain.note: Extensively cultivated in Norfolk; a very reliable cropper.

benoni.heading: BENONI
benoni.flavour: Flesh, yellow, very tender and delicate, sweet, brisk, with a remarkably high perfume, like that of pine apple.
benoni.note: Originated at Dedham, Massachusetts; introduced by Rivers.

edelborsdorfer.heading: BORSDORFER (Borsdorf Hative; Queen's Apple; Red Borsdorfer; Borsdorf; Postophe d'Hiver; Pomme de Prochain; Reinette d'Allemagne; Blanche de Leipsic; Reinette de Misnie; Grand Bohemian Borsdorfer; Garret Pippin; King; King George; King George the Third)
edelborsdorfer.flavour: Flesh, white with a yellowish tinge, crisp and delicate, brisk, juicy, and sugary, and with a rich, vinous, and aromatic flavour.
edelborsdorfer.quality: A dessert apple of the first quality
edelborsdorfer.storage: in use from November to January.
edelborsdorfer.climate: The bloom is very hardy, and withstands the night frosts of spring better than most other varieties.
edelborsdorfer.note: Described as Borsdorfer. Hogg cites Cordus (1561) on its 'sweet and generous flavour, and the pleasant perfume which it exhales'; Diel's 'Pride of the Germans'.

brabant-bellefleur.heading: BRABANT BELLEFLEUR (Glory of Flanders; Iron Apple)
brabant-bellefleur.flavour: Flesh, yellowish white, firm, crisp, and juicy, with a sugary, aromatic, and pleasantly sub-acid flavour.
brabant-bellefleur.quality: An excellent culinary apple of the finest quality
brabant-bellefleur.storage: in use from November to April.
brabant-bellefleur.note: Sent to the Horticultural Society by Booth of Hamburg.

fenouillet-gris.heading: CARAWAY RUSSET
fenouillet-gris.flavour: Flesh, yellowish, firm, crisp, rich, juicy, and sweet, with a very fine aroma.
fenouillet-gris.quality: A dessert apple of great excellence
fenouillet-gris.note: Described under Caraway Russet, which Lindley (1831) lists as a synonym of Fenouillet Gris; Hogg 1884 has no Fenouillet Gris entry, gives no synonym here, does not mention anise, and calls it oblate where his 1851 Fenouillet Gris is roundish-ovate - so probable only. Hogg's Fenouillet Jaune is a different apple.

cellini.heading: CELLINI
cellini.flavour: Flesh, white, tender, very juicy, brisk, and pleasantly flavoured, with a somewhat balsamic aroma.
cellini.quality: A culinary apple of the first quality
cellini.storage: in use during October and November.
cellini.note: Originated with Leonard Phillips of Vauxhall; probably from the Nonesuch.

reinette-rouge-etoilee.heading: EARLY RED CALVILLE (Calville Rouge Precoce)
reinette-rouge-etoilee.flavour: Flesh, tender, pleasantly acid, but not highly flavoured.
reinette-rouge-etoilee.quality: A very ornamental apple, whose greatest recommendation is the brilliancy of its colour.
reinette-rouge-etoilee.storage: It is in use in October and November.
reinette-rouge-etoilee.note: Early Red Calville is an aka in our record; brilliant crimson all over with large fawn russet dots, ornamental, Oct-Nov fits the Sternrenette, but Hogg gives no star/Etoilee synonym, so the identity is not certain.

dutch-mignonne.heading: DUTCH MIGNONNE (Christ's Golden Reinette; Copmanthorpe Crab; Reinette de Caux; Stettin Pippin)
dutch-mignonne.flavour: Flesh, yellow, firm, crisp, very juicy, rich, sweet, and aromatic.
dutch-mignonne.quality: A very valuable and delicious dessert apple
dutch-mignonne.storage: in use from December to April.
dutch-mignonne.note: Hogg describes Grosse Casseler Reinette (an aka in our record) as a separate small second-rate German apple.

frogmore-prolific.heading: FROGMORE PROLIFIC
frogmore-prolific.flavour: Flesh, white, very tender, juicy, and sweet.
frogmore-prolific.quality: Its great merit rests in its cooking qualities, being esteemed one of the finest which is sent into the Royal household at Windsor.
frogmore-prolific.storage: In use from September to Christmas.
frogmore-prolific.note: Raised at Frogmore by Mr. Ingram, the royal gardener. Hogg calls the flesh sweet and says nothing of acidity; our tag is sharp.

gloria-mundi.heading: GLORIA MUNDI (Baltimore; Belle Dubois; Glazenwood Gloria Mundi; Mammoth; Monstrous Pippin; Ox Apple)
gloria-mundi.flavour: Flesh, white, tender, juicy, and, though not highly flavoured, is an excellent culinary apple.
gloria-mundi.storage: It is in use from October to Christmas.
gloria-mundi.note: Hogg doubts the American origin: reported raised by Maszman of Hanover in 1805.

golden-harvey.heading: GOLDEN HARVEY (Brandy Apple; Round Russet Harvey)
golden-harvey.flavour: Flesh, yellow, firm, crisp, juicy, sugary, with an exceedingly rich and powerful aromatic flavour.
golden-harvey.quality: one of the richest and most excellent dessert apples
golden-harvey.storage: in use from December to May, but is very apt to shrivel if exposed to light and air, as most russety apples are.
golden-harvey.note: Also one of the best for cider; juice of specific gravity 1085, hence Brandy Apple. Hogg describes Guernsey Pippin (an aka in our record) as a separate apple.

holland-pippin.heading: HOLLAND PIPPIN
holland-pippin.flavour: Flesh, yellowish white, firm, tender, juicy, sweet, and briskly acid.
holland-pippin.quality: A valuable apple, of first-rate quality for culinary purposes
holland-pippin.storage: it is in use from November to March.
holland-pippin.note: Hogg: the Holland Pippin of Langley and Miller, a native of the Holland district of Lincolnshire, but NOT the Kirton Pippin of Ray and Austen (which is small and oblate) - this contradicts the Kirton Pippin aka in our record.

sweet-bough.heading: LARGE YELLOW BOUGH (Large Early Yellow Bough; Sweet Bough; Early Bough; Bough; Sweet Harvest)
sweet-bough.flavour: Flesh, white, very tender, crisp, and very juicy, with a rich, sweet, sprightly flavour.
sweet-bough.quality: A dessert apple of first-rate quality.
sweet-bough.storage: Ripe in the beginning of August.

lucombes-seedling.heading: LUCOMBE'S SEEDLING
lucombes-seedling.flavour: Flesh, white, firm, juicy, and pleasantly flavoured.
lucombes-seedling.quality: A culinary apple of first-rate quality
lucombes-seedling.storage: in use from October to February.

maiden-blush.heading: MAIDEN'S BLUSH
maiden-blush.flavour: Flesh, white, tender, brisk, and pleasantly acid.
maiden-blush.quality: A very beautiful culinary apple, but not of first-rate quality
maiden-blush.storage: it is in use during September and October.
maiden-blush.note: American apple esteemed round Philadelphia, considered the best for drying; little valued in England.

manningtons-pearmain.heading: MANNINGTON'S PEARMAIN
manningtons-pearmain.flavour: Flesh, yellow, firm, crisp, juicy, and very sugary, with a brisk and particularly rich flavour.
manningtons-pearmain.quality: one of the best and richest flavoured of our dessert apples
manningtons-pearmain.storage: it comes into use in October and November, and continues in good condition till March.
manningtons-pearmain.note: Mannington advised letting the fruit hang late: 'if gathered too soon, it loses much of its fine richness, and is very apt to shrivel'. Originated about 1770 at Uckfield, Sussex.

melon.heading: MELON APPLE
melon.flavour: Flesh, yellowish white, very tender and crisp, juicy, sweet, and vinous, with a delicate and very agreeable perfume.
melon.note: Raised at East Bloomfield, New York - Norton's Melon, so the same as our record (not another Melon homonym).

nanny.heading: NANNY
nanny.flavour: Flesh, yellow, rather soft and tender, juicy, sugary, and highly flavoured.
nanny.quality: A dessert apple of excellent quality, and when in perfection a first-rate fruit
nanny.storage: it is in use during October, but soon becomes mealy.
nanny.note: Resembles Ribston Pippin in flavour; found about Havant, West Sussex.

pine-golden-pippin.heading: PINE GOLDEN PIPPIN
pine-golden-pippin.flavour: Flesh, yellowish white, very tender and juicy, with a fine, sprightly, and distinct pine-apple flavour.
pine-golden-pippin.quality: One of the best dessert apples
pine-golden-pippin.storage: in use during October and November.
pine-golden-pippin.note: Origin untraced; earliest record at Chiswick, sent by Dickson & Son of Hassendean Burn near Hawick.

potts-seedling.heading: POTTS'S SEEDLING
potts-seedling.flavour: Flesh, very tender, and pleasantly sub-acid, with all the character of the flesh of Codlins.
potts-seedling.storage: ripe during September and the early part of October.
potts-seedling.note: Raised by Samuel Potts, Ashton-under-Lyne, about 1849. Hogg describes Deans' Codlin (an aka in our record) separately: a Jedburgh apple in use November to February, so not the same.

reinette-du-canada.heading: REINETTE DE CANADA (Portugal; St. Helena Russet; Canada Reinette)
reinette-du-canada.flavour: Flesh, yellowish white, firm, juicy, brisk, and highly flavoured.
reinette-du-canada.quality: An apple of first-rate quality, either for culinary or dessert use
reinette-du-canada.storage: it is in season from November to April.

williams-favourite.heading: WILLIAMS' FAVOURITE (Williams' Early; Williams' Red)
williams-favourite.flavour: Flesh, white with a greenish tinge, remarkably tender, not very juicy, and with a fine balsamic aroma.
williams-favourite.quality: A very handsome early cooking apple
williams-favourite.storage: ripe in the beginning of August.

ortley.heading: WOOLMAN'S LONG (Ortley; Van Dyne)
ortley.flavour: Flesh, yellowish, crisp, brittle, juicy, with a rich, brisk, and perfumed flavour.
ortley.quality: An excellent apple of first-rate quality, suitable either for culinary or dessert use
ortley.storage: it is in season from December to April.
ortley.note: Described as Woolman's Long; originated in New Jersey.
